Plot methods for the package's results

Source: R/census.R, R/hotspot.R, R/indigenous_frameworks.R, and 8 more
plot-methods.Rd

Every result the package returns draws itself with plot(): no arguments beyond the object are needed, and every method takes the same customisation (main, col or palette, ... for the base-graphics call, the grid from the session option; see plotopt). Titles fit their panel: a title too wide for it is drawn a step smaller, and in a panel set one that still does not fit becomes a letter with the key printed under the panels (the returned data carry it as the plnkey attribute); the left margin is sized from the widest tick label, so an axis title never overlaps the numbers. (Session defaults: see plotopt for the session defaults). Each method returns the data it drew, invisibly, as a data frame.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'rmbl_census_cwb'
plot(
  x,
  ...,
  component = c("cwb", "income", "education", "housing", "labour"),
  main = NULL,
  col = NULL,
  palette = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'rmbl_profile_share'
plot(x, ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, palette = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'rmbl_hotspot'

Arguments

x

The result.

...

Passed to the base-graphics call (plot, barplot or image). They are passed on to each panel's method for a bricklayer_analysis object.

component

For rmbl_census_cwb: "cwb" (the index, default) or one of its components "income", "education", "housing", "labour".

main

Title; each method has a default.

col

Colours, overriding the palette.

palette

A blpal name, overriding the session option.

what

Depends on the class:

  • rmbl_indigenous_gap: "difference" or "ratio";

  • rmbl_stock_flow: the measures to draw (one panel each), any of "adp", "alos", "people", "days", "flowrate", "stkrate";

  • rmbl_yoy: "pctchg" or "value";

  • bricklayer_drift: "psi", "columns", "benford", "ecdf", "quantiles" or "fingerprint";

  • rmbl_case_flow: "flow" and/or "clearance";

  • rmbl_clearance_decomposition: any of "rates", "mix" and "effects" (the default fits the device).

The 0.5.x values "pct_change", "flow_rate" and "stock_rate" are still accepted, as is "rate_change" for which.

points

For rmbl_density, whether to draw the incidents over the surface.

maxparts

For rmbl_clearance_decomposition, the most parts drawn: past it, the parts that moved the aggregate most, and the rest summed into one row. The 0.5.x name max_parts is still accepted.

threshold

For rmbl_balance: the absolute standardised difference drawn as the line of acceptable balance (default 0.1).

after

For rmbl_balance: optionally a second baltab on the same covariates (after weighting or matching), drawn beside the first.

type

For a permutation test: "density" (a kernel density of the permuted statistics, their 5th and 95th percentiles dashed, the observed one in red; the default) or "histogram". For a cross-fitted AIPW result: "overlap" (the weighted distribution of the out-of-fold propensity in each arm with the clipping bounds; the default) or "estimate" (the effect with its confidence interval).

xlab

For the plots over time (rmbl_stock_flow, rmbl_yoy, rmbl_rate_change, rmbl_count_trend, rmbl_event_study, and rmbl_rate with period), the title of the period axis. The default NULL names the unit the period implies: "Date" for dates, "Time" for date-times, "Fiscal year" for fiscal-year labels such as "2022/23", "Periods since adoption" for an event study, otherwise "Period". A number or a date is drawn on its own continuous scale, so a missing period leaves its gap; any other period (text, a factor) is drawn at evenly spaced positions labelled with its text.

gaps

For rmbl_yoy (what = "value") and rmbl_event_study (style = "stata"): how a missing value shows in a line. "break" (the default) breaks the line there, so a "no data" period that yoy(complete = TRUE) inserted is a visible gap; "join" draws the line straight over it.

period

For rmbl_rate, a by column holding the period: the rate is drawn over time with its interval band, one panel per group of the other by columns.

cols

For bricklayer_drift, the columns to draw with what = "columns" or "benford"; NULL (the default) takes up to six, worst first.

warn, fail

For bricklayer_drift, the PSI bands: a column is warn above the first and fail above the second (or when its test rejects at alpha). NULL takes the object's bands.

exposure

For rmbl_crf and rmbl_burden, the exposure range to draw the curve over; the default runs from 0 to 1.5 times the exposure in the object.

contours

Number of contour lines over a field image (0 for none).

which

For bricklayer_analysis, the panels: any of "change", "rates", "ratechg"; NULL draws every panel the analysis has.

style

For an event study: "dot" (filled points with solid capped bars, the default) or "stata" (hollow points joined by a line, dashed capped bars, dashed reference lines).

shadepost

Shade the periods after adoption (default FALSE).

refline

Where the vertical reference line goes (default -0.5, between the reference period and adoption; 0 puts it at adoption).

Value

The data drawn, invisibly. For the plots over time the frame carries the x position of each point drawn: an at column (rmbl_yoy, rmbl_rate_change), or an "at" attribute (rmbl_stock_flow).

Details

rmbl_stock_flow

(stkflow) the average daily population, length of stay, people and person-days over the periods, one panel per measure in what; with an exposure, the flow and stock rates too.

rmbl_yoy

(yoy) the period-over-period percent change with its interval over the periods, the period across and the change up, groups side by side, coloured by verdict; what = "value" draws the values instead.

rmbl_rate, rmbl_share

(rtcalc, shrs) the rate or share per group with its interval.

rmbl_rate_change

(ratechg) the percent change in the rate with its interval over the periods, groups side by side.

rmbl_band_sensitivity

(bandsens) the statistic against the cap applied to the open band.

rmbl_drift_calibration, bricklayer_drift

(drftcal, cpsdrft) the false-alarm rate per column against alpha; for a drift result, what = "psi" (the default) the population stability index per column, worst first, coloured by verdict, with the warn and fail bands as dashed lines; "columns" the reference and current distributions of up to six columns (cols, or the worst), each PSI bin's term written on it; "benford" the first digits of numeric columns against Benford's law with its 95\ test's verdict; "ecdf" both ECDFs with the area between them shaded; "quantiles" the current quantiles against the reference's on the identity line; "fingerprint" one spoke per column, its PSI as the distance out, with the bands as rings.

bricklayer_benford

(benfordtst) observed first-digit proportions against Benford's law.

bricklayer_power

(cpspwr) the power curve: detection rate against injected effect size, with the 0.8 line.

bricklayer_freq, bricklayer_missingness, rmbl_region_coverage

(freqtbl, misspat and rgncov) horizontal bars.

bricklayer_outliers

(mahaoutl) the distance of every row, outliers marked.

bricklayer_correlations, bricklayer_cortable

(topcors, cortbl) the correlation of every pair as a diverging bar.

bricklayer_falsification

(cpsfals) the permutation null distribution with the observed statistic.

rmbl_bounds

(pubbnd) each value inside its published-rounding envelope.

rmbl_indigenous_gap, rmbl_dsr, rmbl_prevalence

each group's difference or ratio, rate, percentage, odds ratio or index with its interval, for these classes and for rmbl_exposure_trend and rmbl_community_index (indgap, agestd, stdprev, exptrnd, commidx); what = "ratio" draws the ratio of a gap.

rmbl_trc_progress

(trcprog) the Calls to Action completed, and the pace projected with the band its interval gives.

rmbl_ordinal_compare

(ordcmp) each group's ratings as one stacked bar, lowest rating on the left.

rmbl_wellness_profile, rmbl_wellness_continuum

wellness indicators above, distress below, each group's estimate and interval (welprof, mhcont).

rmbl_dual_continuum

(dualcont) each group on the two axes, wellness up and distress across.

rmbl_holistic_balance

(holbal) the domains as spokes and each group's levels on them, with its balance.

rmbl_distinctions

(dstntst) each group's estimate and the pooled figure, with I-squared.

rmbl_connection

(connassoc) the places on the two indicators, with their intervals; xlab and ylab name the axes (default: the indicators' column names).

rmbl_healing_change

(healchg) the change in each indicator between the periods, wellness first.

rmbl_profile_share

(profshr) each group's share of a census characteristic with its interval.

rmbl_crf, rmbl_burden, rmbl_equity

and rmbl_pollution_report: in turn, the concentration-response curve with the exposure marked; baseline against attributable cases; the concentration curve of exposure over income rank; and, for a report, all three on one page (crfpm25, polbrdn, expconcidx, vrfpol).

rmbl_footprint

(co2fp) the CPU, memory and total emission in one unit chosen to fit, with the car-kilometre and tree-month equivalents as a caption; "Too short to measure" when the work took no measurable time.

rmbl_field, rmbl_particles

(plmfld, advdif2d, lagrprt) a concentration field as an image with contours; particle positions, with the counting grid behind them when one was given.

rmbl_count_trend

(cnttrnd) the counts with the fitted trend.

bricklayer_analysis

(anltab) the change, rates and rate change of a published table, one panel each.

rmbl_event_study, rmbl_staggered_att

(evstudy, stgatt) the effect at each period since adoption with its interval, the reference period at zero.

rmbl_synth, rmbl_synthdid

(synctl, syndid) the treated unit (or mean) and its synthetic or weighted comparison over time, adoption marked.

rmbl_power

(plnpwr) power against effect size, with the 0.8 line and the minimum detectable effect.

rmbl_prevalence

(stdprev) each group's age-standardised prevalence with its interval.

rmbl_census_cwb

(cnscwb) the Community Well-Being index, or one component, by place, one colour per group.

rmbl_balance

(baltab) a love plot: each covariate's absolute standardised difference against the threshold line, with a second table (after, after weighting or matching) beside it.

rmbl_aipw

(aipwcf) the overlap of the two groups' out-of-fold propensities (type = "overlap") or the estimate with its interval (type = "estimate").

rmbl_event_study, rmbl_staggered_att

also take style = "stata" (hollow points joined by a line, dashed bars) and shadepost; plotevgrid puts several in one grid.

rmbl_bacon

(bacondcmp) each two-group comparison's estimate against its weight, by type, with the two-way estimate.

rmbl_permutation

(perminf) the permuted statistics as a density (5th and 95th percentiles dashed) or histogram, the observed one in red, one panel per outcome.

rmbl_loo, rmbl_cohort_trends

(loounit, cohtrnd) the leave-one-out estimates with the full-sample one; each cohort's outcome by time since adoption.

rmbl_case_flow

(caseflow) cases received and disposed, shaded where the inventory grew or fell, and the clearance rate with its interval and rolling value.

rmbl_life_table

(lifetbl) the share of cases still open at each band edge with its interval, and the median.

rmbl_disposition_mix

(dispmix) the shares of each outcome over the periods, stacked.

rmbl_density

(crmdens) the density of incidents as a heat map, with the highest-density regions outlined.

rmbl_knox

(knoxtst) the Knox ratio of each distance-by-time cell, coloured on a log scale around 1.

rmbl_hotspot

(hotpers) the share of places holding half the incidents and the overlap of hot spots with the period before, over time, and a map of the cells coloured by how often they were hot.

rmbl_svy_estimate, rmbl_svy_compare

(svyest, svycmp) each domain's estimate with its interval, flagged domains marked; each difference from the reference domain with its interval.

rmbl_clearance_decomposition

(clrdcmp) the parts' rates in both comparisons with the aggregate on top, where the workload moved (coloured by whether a part clears above or below the average), and the change as a waterfall of rate and mix effects: the pictures that show a Simpson's-paradox reversal and why it happened.

Examples

sf <- stkflow(days = c(13500, 14600, 15100), people = c(300, 320, 310),
                 prd = 2021:2023)
plot(sf)

plot(sf, what = "alos", col = "firebrick", main = "Length of stay")

y <- yoy(data.frame(year = 2019:2023, n = c(400, 420, 390, 460, 450)), value = "n",
         prd = "year")
plot(y)

# small counts: each percentage carries its exact interval
plot(yoy(data.frame(year = 2019:2023, n = c(10, 12, 11, 15, 14)), value = "n",
         prd = "year"))

plot(benfordtst(c(1, 12, 123, 1234, 2, 23, 3, 31, 4, 45, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9)))

plot(crfno2(25))

plot(co2fp(for (i in 1:20) sum(sqrt(seq_len(2e5))), loc = "CA",
                       cpupwrw = 45, memgb = 8))

# the courts and crime data shipped with the package
ext <- function(f) {
  read.csv(system.file("extdata", f, package = "rmoriebricklayer"))
}
fl <- ext("ocj_flow_ontario.csv")
plot(caseflow(fl$received, fl$disposed, pend = fl$pending, prd = fl$month))

td <- ext("ocj_time_to_disposition.csv")
open <- unlist(td[nrow(td), 2:5]) * fl$disposed[nrow(fl)]
plot(lifetbl(c(0, 10, 15, 18, Inf), open))

dm <- ext("ocj_dispositions.csv")
plot(dispmix(dm[, -(1:2)], prd = dm$year))

og <- ext("ocj_offence_groups.csv")
og <- og[og$year %in% c(2014, 2022), ]
plot(clrdcmp(og$disposed, og$received, og$offence_group, og$year))

be <- ext("tps_break_enter_d14_2024.csv")
be <- be[!is.na(be$lon), ]
plot(crmdens(be$lon, be$lat, ngrid = 60))

# \donttest{
plot(knoxtst(be$lon, be$lat, as.Date(be$occ_date), c(100, 200, 400), c(7, 14, 28),
               nsim = 99, seed = 1))

# }
plot(hotpers(be$lon, be$lat, quarters(as.Date(be$occ_date)), cell = 0.3))

# rates, shares and the change in a rate
rt <- data.frame(division = rep(c("n", "e", "w"), 2), year = rep(2022:2023, each = 3),
                 stops = c(120, 90, 60, 150, 85, 70),
                 residents = rep(c(1e4, 8e3, 5e3), 2))
r23 <- rt[rt$year == 2023, ]
plot(rtcalc(r23, count = "stops", pop = "residents", by = "division"))

plot(shrs(r23, count = "stops", by = "division"))

plot(ratechg(rt, count = "stops", pop = "residents", prd = "year",
                 by = "division"))

# a rate over time, one panel per group
plot(rtcalc(rt, count = "stops", pop = "residents", by = c("division", "year")),
     period = "year")

# complex survey estimates by domain, and the differences between domains
set.seed(3)
sv <- data.frame(region = rep(c("north", "south", "east"), length.out = 300),
                 smoker = rbinom(300, 1, 0.25), w = runif(300, 50, 150))
sd <- svydes(sv, w = "w", strata = "region")
plot(svyest(sd, sv, "smoker", by = "region", stat = "proportion", lvls = "1"))

plot(svycmp(sd, sv, "smoker", by = "region", stat = "proportion", lvls = "1"))

# a published table in one call: change, rates and rate change
tab <- data.frame(year = rep(2020:2023, each = 2), g = rep(c("a", "b"), 4),
                  n = c(10, 20, 12, 22, 11, 25, 15, 24), pop = rep(c(1000, 2000), 4))
plot(anltab(tab, value = "n", prd = "year", by = "g", pop = "pop"))

plot(cnttrnd(c(21000, 23000, 22000, 25000, 24000)))

# banded tables
plot(bandsens(prsbands(c("0-17", "18-24", "25-44", "45+")), c(10, 20, 30, 40),
                      caps = c(60, 70, 80, 90)))

plot(pubbnd(c(10, 20), rnd = 5))

plot(rgncov(c("a", "b", "c"), c(100, 200, 300), c(1L, 0L, 2L)))

# drift between two extracts, and how often the test cries wolf
set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(a = rnorm(400), b = sample(letters[1:3], 400, TRUE))
dr <- cpsdrft(dd, transform(dd, a = a + 3))
plot(dr)

plot(dr, what = "columns")

plot(dr, what = "benford", warn = 0.05, fail = 0.2)

plot(dr, what = "ecdf")

plot(dr, what = "quantiles")

plot(dr, what = "fingerprint")

plot(drftcal(dd, n = 20L))

# describing a table
plot(freqtbl(data.frame(g = c("a", "b", "b", "c", "c", "c")), "g"))

plot(misspat(data.frame(a = c(1, NA, 3, NA), b = c(NA, NA, 1, 2))))

hw <- data.frame(h = rnorm(100), w = rnorm(100))
hw$h[1] <- 15
plot(mahaoutl(hw))

sq <- data.frame(a = 1:20, b = (1:20)^2, c = rev(1:20))
plot(topcors(sq))

plot(cortbl(sq))

# power and falsification of a statistic
xy <- data.frame(x = rnorm(60), y = rnorm(60))
shift <- function(z, s) {
  z$y <- z$y + s * z$x
  z
}
plot(cpspwr(xy, function(z) cor(z$x, z$y), inject = shift, trt = "x",
                   sizes = c(0, 0.25, 0.5), n = 19, reps = 3, seed = 1))

plot(cpsfals(xy, function(z) cor(z$x, z$y), trt = "x", n = 29, seed = 1))

plot(polbrdn(25, 1, 0.008, 1e6, poll = "NO2"))

plot(expconcidx(data.frame(exposure = c(4, 1, 8, 2),
                                             income = c(2, 1, 4, 3)),
                                  "exposure", "income"))

plot(vrfpol("no2", demo = TRUE))

plot(lagrprt(200, 0, 0, 1, 0.5, 1, 1, 1, 20,
                          grid = c(-10, 40, -15, 25, 10, 8)))

                 y = seq(-300, 300, by = 50)))
